solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Page taking another right turn around vault (8)

indicators.note: LEAF takes P in, holding it inside
GO is turned round to read OG

blocks.note: a leaf is a page of a book
another page, abbreviated P, goes inside LEAF
R = right
a go is a turn in a game

annotation.surface: A page boy takes another right turn on his way round a burial vault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a noun (a crypt), but it is the playground game in which you vault over a crouching friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a game of vaulting over others, and also a verb meaning to vault over.

entries.clue: Runaway inmate stops here at last to cover head (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the words before it
the outer letters wrap around, covering, the next piece

blocks.note: last letters of inmatE, stopS, herE
a cape or head is a headland, as in Beachy Head

annotation.surface: A prison story: the runaway inmate's journey finally ends here, head hidden under a hood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runaway inmate' reads as one phrase, but only 'Runaway' is the definition; 'inmate' is the first of the three words whose last letters are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A runaway, as a noun, is someone who has fled, which is an escapee.

entries.clue: Blunt scheme collecting one small parking fine inside of Kent (5-6)

indicators.note: PLAN gathers I into itself
only the inner letters of Kent are used

blocks.note: a scheme is a plan
one = I, the Roman numeral, placed inside PLAN
S = small, as on clothing labels
P = parking, as on road signs
fine = OK
the middle letters of KENT

annotation.surface: A heavy-handed scheme to collect small parking fines within Kent, a county in south-east England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not a penalty here, despite the parking; it simply means OK.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone plain-spoken says things bluntly, without softening them.

entries.clue: What flows up through hollow rusty piping (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece reads from the bottom, backwards
the reversed river runs through the other letters, sitting inside them
rusty with its middle emptied leaves only its outer letters

blocks.note: the Dee is a river, a thing that flows
the outer letters of RUSTY

annotation.surface: Water trickling up through a corroded, empty old pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piping' seems to be plumbing to match 'rusty', but it is an adjective for a high, thin voice.
annotation.definitionFit: A piping voice is high and thin, which is what a reedy voice is.

entries.clue: Cook’s high-quality cheese with 40 per cent off king paid for (7)

indicators.note: two of GOUDA's five letters, 40 per cent, are cut off the end

blocks.note: GOUDA, a Dutch cheese, less its last two letters
R = rex, king
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met = paid for

annotation.surface: A cook's fine cheese, marked down forty per cent, is bought by the king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook's high-quality' reads as the start of a story, but it defines the answer: gourmet food is the high-quality kind a cook serves.
annotation.definitionFit: Gourmet, as an adjective, describes high-quality food for discerning eaters and cooks.

entries.clue: Engage contractors with globe (6)

blocks.note: abs, the abdominal muscles, contract
an orb is a globe

annotation.surface: Hiring builders to work on a globe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contractors' suggests builders, but here it means muscles, which are the body's contractors.
annotation.definitionFit: To engage someone's attention is to absorb them in something.

entries.clue: Disdain old guy’s first shown in island church (9)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of guy
OG appears inside the island's name

blocks.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland
O = old
the first letter of GUY; O and G go inside ARRAN
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: An old man's scorn, shown first in a little island church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old guy's first' splits in two: 'old' gives O on its own and 'first' applies only to guy, so OG, not just G, goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt for others, which is arrogance.

entries.clue: Type of music request when cycling (3)

indicators.note: the letters of ASK rotate, the first letter moving to the end

blocks.note: to request is to ask

annotation.surface: Asking for a song while riding a bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' sounds like bicycles; it means moving the first letter to the back.
annotation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican style of music, forerunner of reggae.

entries.clue: Whistler may display this in town close to Sunderland (3,4)

indicators.note: the close, or end, of Sunderland is its last letter

blocks.note: Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England
the last letter of SUNDERLAND

annotation.surface: A whistling painter shows off his work in a town near Sunderland, a city in north-east England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' invites the painter James Whistler, but it is a football referee, who blows a whistle and shows a red card.
annotation.definitionFit: A referee, the whistler, holds up a red card to send a player off.

entries.clue: Cut in drab uniform fixed after two drinks (13)

indicators.note: the letters are fixed, as in repaired, into a new order
the rearranged letters come after the two drinks

blocks.note: CHA, slang for tea, then TEA itself
IN + DRAB + U (uniform in the phonetic alphabet), rearranged

annotation.surface: A soldier in a dull uniform, tidied up after a couple of drinks, gets a haircut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a trim, but it is a cut of meat: the thick centre of a beef fillet.
annotation.definitionFit: Chateaubriand is a thick cut from the tenderloin of beef.

entries.clue: Just about record somersaulting in public (6)

indicators.note: ONLY goes around the next piece
a somersault turns EP head over heels, to PE

blocks.note: just = only
an EP is an extended-play record; reversed and put inside ONLY

annotation.surface: An acrobat very nearly sets a tumbling record in front of a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just about' looks like one phrase meaning nearly, but 'Just' is ONLY and 'about' says it goes round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is done in public is done where all can see, not in secret.

entries.clue: Celebrity recalled some philosopher at sage meeting (8)

indicators.note: called back, so the letters read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are used

blocks.note: philosopheR AT SAGE Meeting, read backwards

annotation.surface: A famous figure remembers a gathering where a thinker met a wise man.
annotation.walkthrough: The thinkers are there only to carry letters; a megastar is about as far from a sage as the clue gets.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with MEGA- adding scale: a star of the biggest kind is a celebrity.

entries.clue: Means of driving forward, except for earlier Tesla models (11)

indicators.note: remove the earlier of the two Ts in STIMULATIONS

blocks.note: stimulations spur things on
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density; the first T is removed

annotation.surface: Talk of how cars are driven, apart from Tesla's early models.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, with 'models' and 'driving' to match; here it is the scientific unit, symbol T.
annotation.definitionFit: Simulations are models that imitate how something behaves.

entries.clue: Port resident docked close to ace pilot flying north (10)

indicators.note: NEAR has its tail docked, cut off
the letters are sent flying into a new order

blocks.note: close to = NEAR, minus its last letter
A (ace, as on playing cards) + PILOT, rearranged
N = north

annotation.surface: A harbour resident has moored by a top pilot who flies northwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Docked' wants to belong to the port, but it trims the word after it. 'Resident' belongs with 'Port' in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan lives in Naples, a port city in southern Italy.

entries.clue: One working for lender in Iran worked with Blair (9)

indicators.note: the letters are worked, as in kneaded, into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, mixed in with IRAN

annotation.surface: A bank employee in Iran collaborated with Tony Blair, the former British prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lender' suggests a bank, but a library lends books.
annotation.definitionFit: A librarian works for a library, an institution that lends books.

entries.clue: Government department introducing current PM (4)

blocks.note: MOD = Ministry of Defence
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A ministry introduces the sitting prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like it qualifies PM, meaning the present one, but it is I. Narendra Modi is prime minister of India.
annotation.definitionFit: Narendra Modi is a PM, India's prime minister.

entries.clue: A lot of muck on left side of Kelvin’s Highland sticker (4)

indicators.note: most, but not all, of DIRT is used
in an across word the left side is the first letter

blocks.note: DIRT less its last letter
the first letter of KELVIN

annotation.surface: Mud all over the left side of Kelvin's Scottish souvenir sticker.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'sticker' sounds like a label, but it is something you stick people with: a dirk is a Scottish Highland dagger.
annotation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long dagger traditionally carried in the Scottish Highlands.

entries.clue: Six blocking opening that’s artificially produced (2,5)

indicators.note: VI sits in the way, inside the opening

blocks.note: an intro is the opening of a piece
VI is six in Roman numerals, placed inside INTRO

annotation.surface: A cricket six blocks an opening that was manufactured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artificially produced' is an adjective phrase, and IN VITRO works the same way, as in in vitro fertilisation.
annotation.definitionFit: In vitro means made in a test tube or dish, outside the body, so artificially produced.

entries.clue: Male band saving time with Bill’s great deal (6-4)

indicators.note: ELO keeps, saves, T inside it

blocks.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, a British rock band
T = time, placed inside ELO
a bill, a poster, is an advertisement, an AD

annotation.surface: A boy band saves time while getting a bargain from Bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill's' reads as possessive, but the 's is just 'is': Bill is (the) great deal.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: as much as a bucket holds stands for a large amount.

entries.clue: Natives of foreign ancestry broadcast scoreline having lost at home (7)

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, like seed broadcast over a field
IN is taken out of the letters first

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, once IN is gone
to be in is to be at home; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: A foreign-born team's supporters hear a result read out after an away defeat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' seems to go with the scoreline on the radio, but it only rearranges letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Creoles are people born in the Caribbean or Americas of European or mixed ancestry.

entries.clue: Did Harry duck Yankee visiting old queen and duke? (7)

indicators.note: O and Y come to stay inside ANNE

blocks.note: Queen Anne reigned in the early 1700s
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
Yankee is Y in the phonetic alphabet; O and Y go inside ANNE
D = duke

annotation.surface: A royal question: did Prince Harry dodge an American visiting the old queen and a duke?
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince, surrounded by queens and dukes, but 'harry' is a verb meaning to pester, so 'Did Harry' means annoyed.
annotation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass them, so 'did harry' is annoyed.

entries.clue: Eggs on hosts smashing new dishes (8)

indicators.note: one piece placed next to the other
OVA holds the next piece inside it
something smashed is broken into pieces, so the letters of new lose their order

blocks.note: ova are eggs
NEW rearranged, placed inside OVA
re = on, concerning

annotation.surface: Someone egging on party hosts to smash the new crockery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as a verb, urging; it is really OVA + RE, with 'on' doing double duty as the RE.
annotation.definitionFit: Ovenware is heat-proof dishes for cooking in the oven.

entries.clue: Affectionate daughter books popular centre for vigil (6)

indicators.note: only the middle letter of vigil is used

blocks.note: D = daughter
OT = Old Testament, a set of books
in = popular, fashionable
the middle letter of VIGIL

annotation.surface: A loving daughter reserves a well-liked venue for a candlelit vigil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb, reserving a venue; it is OT.
annotation.definitionFit: Doting means fondly, excessively affectionate.

entries.clue: Old bit of school out of bounds (5)

indicators.note: EDUCATE's bounds, its first and last letters, are taken out

blocks.note: to school someone is to educate them; drop the E at each end

annotation.surface: A former part of a school that pupils are no longer allowed into.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like a part, but it is a coin, as in a threepenny bit, an old British coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A ducat was an old gold or silver coin, so an old bit of money.

entries.clue: Part of terrorist organisation isn’t backing Mike in play Operation (13)

indicators.note: CELL and IS NOT together are read backwards
Mike is in play, literally placed within the letters of TOY

blocks.note: a terrorist group is organised in cells
isn't expanded to IS NOT
to play is to toy
Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet, placed inside TOY

annotation.surface: A terrorist cell refuses to back Mike in a play called 'Operation'.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital O makes 'Operation' look like a title, but it is a surgical operation. 'Isn't' must be spelt out as IS NOT before reversing.
annotation.definitionFit: A tonsillectomy is the surgical operation to remove the tonsils.

entries.clue: Granny periodically reared Jade (3)

indicators.note: take every other letter, at regular periods
in a down clue, reared means raised up, read from the bottom

blocks.note: the odd letters of GrAnNy

annotation.surface: Grandmother, from time to time, brought up a girl named Jade.
annotation.walkthrough: Jade reads as a girl's name, but a jade is a worn-out old horse, which is a nag.
annotation.definitionFit: A jade is an old, worn-out horse, which is also called a nag.

entries.clue: Bean drink paired with game (6)

blocks.note: nog is an egg-based drink, as in eggnog
gin rummy, the card game, is often just gin

annotation.surface: A coffee bean drink served with a game of cards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bean' looks like coffee, but it is slang for the head, as is noggin.
annotation.definitionFit: Bean and noggin are both informal words for the head.

entries.clue: Reserve awkwardly eats second fish (3,5)

indicators.note: the letters of eats are arranged awkwardly, out of order

blocks.note: EATS rearranged
S = second
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

annotation.surface: A substitute player clumsily eats a second helping of fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a noun, a substitute player, but it is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: keeping something back for later use.
